entries.title: Treasury and IRS finalize backup withholding rules for third party network transactions, effective immediately
entries.facts: Treasury and the IRS published final regulations (TD 10053, RIN 1545-BR80, 91 FR 51391) governing backup withholding under Internal Revenue Code section 3406 on reportable payments with respect to third party network transactions. The regulations are effective August 10, 2026 and apply with respect to payments made in calendar years beginning after December 31, 2024. Under the final rules, for payments made in settlement of third party network transactions the amount subject to withholding is determined with regard to the de minimis exception for third party settlement organizations in section 6050W(e): a payment is treated as a reportable payment only if, during the calendar year, the aggregate number of transactions with respect to the participating payee exceeds the number specified in section 6050W(e)(2) and the aggregate amount of all reportable payment transactions exceeds the dollar amount specified in section 6050W(e)(1). The preamble examples use 200 transactions and $20,000. The regulations adopt the January 9, 2026 proposed rules without change and implement section 70432(b)(1) of Public Law 119-21.
entries.relevant_to: payment platforms, online marketplaces, payment apps and other third party settlement organizations

entries.title: FTC obtains court order temporarily halting Credit Glory credit repair operation
entries.facts: The Federal Trade Commission announced that, at its request, a federal court has temporarily halted a credit repair scheme run by a network of 17 related companies and their principals. The FTC's complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona following a 2-0 Commission vote, alleges that since at least 2016 Credit Glory and related entities made false and misleading promises about their credit repair services, impersonated debt collection entities and creditors, collected illegal upfront fees, and charged illegal advance fees on a recurring basis using a negative option without clearly disclosing the recurring fees, taking nearly $200 million from consumers. The FTC alleges violations of the FTC Act, the Credit Repair Organizations Act, the Telemarketing Sales Rule, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. The FTC notes that it files a complaint when it has reason to believe the named defendants are violating or are about to violate the law, and that the case will be decided by the court.
entries.source_label: Federal Trade Commission press release, August 10, 2026
entries.relevant_to: credit repair and consumer finance operators, subscription and negative-option billing platforms, telemarketers

entries.title: CFTC Innovation Advisory Committee sets inaugural meeting for August 20, 2026
entries.facts: CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig, sponsor of the Innovation Advisory Committee, announced that the IAC will hold its inaugural meeting at 1 p.m. EST on August 20, 2026 in Washington. The release states the Innovation Advisory Committee was created to advise the Commission on complex issues at the intersection of technology, law, policy and finance, and that the committee will provide insights and recommendations to the Commission to help ensure its regulations keep pace with the speed of innovation on what the release calls the new frontier of finance. The meeting will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov, and dial-in and webinar details are published in the release. The CFTC notes that the views expressed by its advisory committees are solely those of the respective committee and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government.
entries.relevant_to: digital asset firms, derivatives and event-contract platforms, fintech firms engaging with the CFTC
